2026-10-24 Italy

Rome Day 1

Rachel here!

Toronto airport

We met at the Toronto airport - Rachel coming from her conference in Niagara Falls and Sebas from home.

At the airport
At the airport

We made it

The 8 hr flight went smoothly, and we arrived in Rome tired but excited.

We made it to Rome!

To the hotel

We took the airport train to the main station in Rome, which is just a few minutes walk from our hotel.

We can't escape Canada - the first store we saw upon arriving to the station.

The hotel

The hotel is on the second floor of the building, with the tiniest, sketchiest elevator either of us has seen.

The elevator
The elevator has barely enough room for one person and two suitcases.
The beautiful ceiling of the hotel hallway - much nicer than the elevator

Lunch

After dropping our stuff at the hotel, we went for lunch at a nearby restaurant recommended by the hotel receptionist.

Bruschetta
Sebas ordered a grilled seafood plate (Grigliata di Mare).
I got a pasta!
At the restaurant

Walking around Rome

After lunch, we went for a walk to see some of the famous historical sites. There were so many gorgeous churches all over the city. We had one on the itinerary, but just happened to find 3 or 4 more with beautiful paintings and statues.

There are so many beautiful fountains. We just stumbled upon this one.
A church
Sebas at the church
Super intricate carvings on a street corner.
Statue on a street corner.
So many cute tiny cars!
Walking around Rome
Even tinier car!
Walking around Rome

Spanish Steps

Our first stop was the Spanish Steps. Rome seems a little...culturally confused. We visited the Spanish Steps, which were built by the French kings because it is close to the Vatican. At the top of the steps was an Egyptian obelisk. And all this was in Italy.

Egyptian obelisk

The Pantheon

Then we visited the Pantheon. This site was a Roman Temple since 27BC, then this building was built as a new temple in 118AD. It was converted into a church in 609AD, and they still run services there!

The Pantheon
At the Pantheon
The Pantheon from the other side
This moment felt like everything we expected Italy to be: music, beautiful architecture, ancient buildings

Piazza Navonna

Our final stop was Piazza Navonna, a big square, and what used to be the site of a Roman stadium.

We were initially annoyed at the way this ad ruined the vibe of the beautiful square. Then we realized the scantily clad models are just the modern version of the naked statues in the fountain.
